headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Goose can write/egress broadly while next-ai-draw-io ingests files and uses external model APIs by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose has filesystem write and MCP access, and next-ai-draw-io processes user files and natural-language commands. A shared workspace or file handoff lets attacker-controlled diagram/text content influence Goose through copied outputs or MCP-mediated flows. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or file tree
IF next-ai-draw-io content is copied into Goose prompts or MCP inputs
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Require manual review of any file content before Goose consumes it
Use read-only mounts for next-ai-draw-io inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose reads and writes the user filesystem and has broad network egress; next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and diagrams and can call multiple external model APIs. If they share files or credentials, sensitive document contents can flow from Goose-managed files into next-ai-draw-io’s outbound API calls, creating an exfiltration path in default workflows.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or document set
IF next-ai-draw-io sends those documents to a remote model provider
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Disable remote model providers in next-ai-draw-io
Run Goose with a dedicated least-privilege account
Use separate API keys per agent
requires-engineering: add DLP or content redaction before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to files and use MCP, and Goose explicitly shares state via the filesystem across instances. next-ai-draw-io also handles files and can operate concurrently. Without locking, simultaneous edits to the same diagrams, text files, or project files can overwrite each other or corrupt state, especially when Goose also modifies git state.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same repository or directory
IF either agent writes while the other is reading or transforming the same file
mitigations: Assign disjoint file paths per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git branches for Goose edits
Avoid concurrent runs on the same workspace
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code or file changes that next-ai-draw-io may then ingest as authoritative diagram/text input. next-ai-draw-io is designed for AI-assisted visualization and can act on natural-language commands, so an unverified Goose output can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream API-driven transformations. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles.
conditions: IF Goose output is used as the source of truth for diagrams or document transformations
IF next-ai-draw-io is allowed to proceed without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before next-ai-draw-io acts on Goose output
Compare Goose output against source files before use
Limit Goose to drafting only
Log and diff all generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add validation rules between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Goose handles model provider keys and extension tokens, while next-ai-draw-io handles API keys and can route content to multiple third-party model providers. That creates a compliance mismatch risk around retention and data residency for the same documents, especially if sensitive files are processed by remote providers. The profiles do not show a shared compliance boundary, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive documents are processed by next-ai-draw-io
IF remote model providers retain prompts or outputs beyond the operator’s policy
mitigations: Restrict both agents to non-sensitive data
Choose providers with matching retention terms
Document a shared data-handling policy
Rotate and scope API keys separately
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention enforcement
